concepts.title: The program
concepts.blurb: How can a powerful reasoner improve without treating every correction as an attack? One plan with seven lines, indexed by the argument map; every registered claim, item, decision and round hangs under it.

concepts.title: Normativity
concepts.blurb: What it means for a changing reasoner to remain responsive to reasons. A fixed objective scores behavior from outside; this line builds obligation, answer and enforcement as machine-checkable structure instead.

concepts.title: Legitimacy
concepts.blurb: The bridge between normativity and deference: normative learning needs public reasons, and responses that carry standing rather than mere compliance. Its spine is the record half (Integrity) and the licence half (warrants).

concepts.title: Deference and trust
concepts.blurb: How a bounded reasoner benefits from a better-informed process without surrendering the ability to correct what that process does. 'Trust' names several distinct relations; the line separates and connects them.

concepts.title: Corrigibility
concepts.blurb: Corrigibility from response authority: the corrigibility kernel's headline is specification-layer, with legitimate activated evaluation as its principal value and continuation BRIA as its learning layer.

concepts.title: Openness and non-capture
concepts.blurb: Robust Openness at a state, defined over application-supplied coverage data: the reasoner remains correctable by parties it has not captured, certified rather than assumed.

concepts.title: Normative induction
concepts.blurb: The thread that makes normative learning inductive: the Progress statistic, the edge-local practical certificate, and the finite three-term bound on the accounted export.

concepts.title: Normative Inductor
concepts.blurb: The line's central machine: Logical Induction over an assessment process with projection enforcement, preserved under the operations the practice needs. Canonical architecture; conditional theorems.

concepts.title: Enforcement compiler
concepts.blurb: The construction that turns obligations into price movements: enforcement as convex projection of a credal state, with a typed outcome that conserves what was owed. Its three narrow results are lean-proved.

concepts.title: Finite-date conformance
concepts.blurb: A conformance bound at a date, where logical induction's inexploitability criterion gives only an asymptotic guarantee — the program's finite-time strengthening of its own substrate.

concepts.title: Warrant licence chain
concepts.blurb: A licensed verdict is supported on the record's grounds and admissible in their settled region: the chain from an announced verdict back through its warrant to the accounted record.

concepts.title: Normative record
concepts.blurb: The left side of normative learning: what determines why a demand arose, how evidence enters the practice, and what a learner answers to — an identity-bearing record of obligations and responses.

concepts.title: Settlement interface
concepts.blurb: Six distinct conditions, each with one home: four typed inputs of the protocol, two consequences or clauses of theorems elsewhere. The seam between a record and what counts as settled against it.

concepts.title: Normative seed
concepts.blurb: The left-most object of the record picture made concrete: what a reasoner starts from and what it forces on the prices of a settled region.

concepts.title: Defeat with a named successor
concepts.blurb: A defeated obligation is answered or disposed — and disposal carries the debt to a named successor rather than extinguishing it. Authored, history-sensitive answerability under defeat; the future depends on which defaults lost.

concepts.title: Answerability score
concepts.blurb: The static question: what makes a reason, challenge or response publicly assessable before any learning happens? The score is that assessability made a quantity.

concepts.title: Diachronic answerability
concepts.blurb: What the record half of legitimacy — an open Integrity ledger — amounts to over time: answerability as a property of a history, derived rather than postulated.

concepts.title: Integrity
concepts.blurb: The record's conservation package: what was owed is satisfied, disposed of, or remaining. The conservation theorem, propagation law, receipt immutability, faithful carry and multiplicity witness are lean-proved.

concepts.title: Continuation BRIA
concepts.blurb: Bounded inductive rationality lifted from one-step choices to temporally extended continuations, without counterfactual reward tables and without surrendering correctability.

concepts.title: Serviceability
concepts.blurb: When obligations can be served on time: exact rational fixtures for timely service, with the optimality of serving oldest first and the transfer of service-weighted convergence to obligation-weighted.

concepts.title: Liability and affordability
concepts.blurb: Who pays for enforcement and what a practice can afford: the enforcement layer's three narrow results are lean-proved; the liability theory over them is open realization material.

concepts.title: Progress statistic
concepts.blurb: The statistic that says a practice is getting somewhere: paper-derived research under normative induction, with the finite bound on accounted export as its Established core.

concepts.title: Effective authority layer
concepts.blurb: The deference line's authority cluster: one informal claim established by twelve declarations — authority and sincerity conditions under which a verdict-giver's standing is effective rather than nominal.

concepts.title: Robust openness certificate
concepts.blurb: A sufficient external certificate yields Robust Openness at a state: the split bill is the certificate, and the equivalence sits on the legitimacy spine.

concepts.title: Finite delegation bridge
concepts.blurb: The finite bridge from a local delegation to the deference line: what a bounded delegator can check locally and still inherit from the delegate's guarantee.

concepts.title: Actionability and normative force
concepts.blurb: What makes a requirement actionable — force as what enforcement does to prices, not as metaphor. The action theory over the lean-proved enforcement results is open.

concepts.title: Deontic scorekeeping
concepts.blurb: Brandom: normative status instituted by practice through tracked commitments and entitlements, attributing distinguished from acknowledging. It gives the architecture its shape without importing inferentialist semantics.

concepts.title: Reasons as defaults
concepts.blurb: Horty's treatment of a reason's weight and priority as normative content rather than machinery. A static theory: default logic says what to conclude, not what is owed, and its proper scenarios forget the history of defeats.

concepts.title: Rebutting and undercutting defeat
concepts.blurb: Pollock's distinction between attacking a conclusion and attacking the support itself — a genuine dependency here, transposed from a belief's warrant to a debt's.

concepts.title: Exclusionary reasons
concepts.blurb: Raz: a second-order reason not to act on certain first-order reasons. In Horty's own rendering they remain challengeable in-system, which puts exclusion closer to disposition than to settlement.

concepts.title: Practical authority
concepts.blurb: Authority as standing to change what someone owes, as against power to change what they do. The program renders it as record-readable entitlement rather than as a property of persons.

concepts.title: Logical induction
concepts.blurb: Garrabrant et al. 2016: a sequence of prices for logical claims that no polynomial trader can exploit. The market, the traders, the market maker and the inexploitability criterion are the substrate the enforcement construction is built on.

concepts.title: Imprecise probability
concepts.blurb: Coherent lower and upper previsions, sets of probabilities, and the linear-feasibility characterization of probabilistic entailment. The credal state is one; the enforced regions are convex sets of probabilities.

concepts.title: Convex projection
concepts.blurb: Projection onto a convex set and its defining variational inequality — the enforcement direction, used as a genuine dependency.

concepts.title: LP duality and Farkas certificates
concepts.blurb: The finite-horizon infeasibility certificate has the shape of a Farkas pair and is called one, but its soundness proof is four self-contained lines; exactness under a Slater point is what actually leans on duality.

concepts.title: Interval feasibility
concepts.blurb: Gale–Hoffman flow feasibility, and directly Horn's 1974 conditions for preemptive scheduling with release times and deadlines. The transport-onto-service-dates condition cites this theorem rather than proving it.

concepts.title: Contiguity of measures
concepts.blurb: Le Cam 1960. The condition under which service-weighted convergence transfers to obligation-weighted convergence is contiguity in exactly this sense — the definition inherited, the proof direct.

concepts.title: Earliest-due-date scheduling
concepts.blurb: Jackson 1955: serve the oldest obligation first. The optimality argument here is the same exchange argument, classical in substance, written out in four self-contained lines.

concepts.title: Truth-maintenance systems
concepts.blurb: Doyle 1979, de Kleer 1986: dependency-directed, identity-bearing justification structure with the environment/label separation that lets several stances be held at once — the record's structural ancestor.

concepts.title: Structured argumentation (ASPIC+)
concepts.blurb: Attack and defeat over structured arguments with reinstatement computed by the semantics. No successor and an unauthored attack relation — the contrast that locates what the defeat theory here adds.

concepts.title: Cartesian frames
concepts.blurb: Garrabrant's factorizations of a world into agent and environment as a pair of sets with a matrix between them — the embedded-agency agenda's algebra of where an agent's boundary sits.

concepts.title: Updateless decision theory
concepts.blurb: Deciding from the policy level without updating on observations first — the decision-theory thread of agent foundations that extended-choice constructions here deliberately avoid needing.

concepts.title: Brandom, Making It Explicit (1994)
concepts.blurb: The source of deontic scorekeeping: norms instituted by social practice, commitment and entitlement tracked by scorekeepers.

concepts.title: Horty, Reasons as Defaults (2012)
concepts.blurb: The default-logic account of reasons checked against its own text here: no ledger for what is owed, no history-sensitivity, authority only as the content of a default — read as the nearest static theory, not imported.

concepts.title: Embedded Agency (Demski & Garrabrant)
concepts.blurb: The agenda whose questions — bounded reasoners embedded in, and smaller than, the world they reason about — this program approaches through normativity rather than through decision theory.

concepts.title: Corrigibility (Soares et al. 2015)
concepts.blurb: The paper that posed shutdown and correction as a formal problem and showed the naive utility patches fail — the historical motivation the corrigibility line answers with response authority instead.

concepts.title: Deconfusing Corrigibility (post)
concepts.blurb: The post whose formal content — Definitions through Learning with logical induction — is one Lean file in this repository, registered as its companion formalization.

concepts.title: Formalized Agent Foundations
concepts.blurb: The pinned Lean library carrying the logical-induction formalization this repository builds against; the pin is part of the trust chain, moved only by a verified bump.
